sections.content: How many people are "managers in transport and distribution"?

95,715 people

were counted on the census as "managers in transport and distribution" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Managers in transport and distribution organise and co-ordinate the activities and resources necessary for the safe, efficient and economic movement of passengers and freight by road, rail, sea and air transport.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "managers in transport and distribution" there were more men than women (80.7% compared with 19.3%).

This means "managers in transport and distribution" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 80.7% and women made up 19.3% of "managers in transport and distribution"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "managers in transport and distribution" included:

  • farmers
  • IT operations technicians
  • managers in storage and warehousing

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "managers in transport and distribution", 15.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "managers in transport and distribution" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "managers in transport and distribution" included:

  • office managers
  • crane drivers
  • waste disposal and environmental services managers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "managers in transport and distribution" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "managers in transport and distribution" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "managers in transport and distribution", 7.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (87.2% compared with 12.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (81.9%) than self-employed (18.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
